inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E (year to 30-Sep-2026, closed but not yet reported). 9M FY26 actual revenue $2,060.2M (Q1 685.8 + Q2 774.3 + Q3 600.0) plus an estimated Q4 of ~$820M (Q4 FY25 was $894M; Q4 is the seasonal peak under ASC-606 upfront term-licence recognition, less ~$40M/qtr of divested Kepware/ThingWorx). FY2025 actual was $2,739.2M. FY0 is FY26E rather than FY25 because the June-2026 balance sheet already contains nine months of FY26 cash flow; projecting FY26 as year 1 would count that cash twice.
inputs.share_count_basis: 108.51M basic shares on the 10-Q Q3 FY26 cover (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding, 2026-07-29) plus ~0.9M dilutive RSUs (Q3 FY26 diluted-vs-basic gap). Held FLAT: SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-charge. The count has fallen sharply (120.8M FY25 diluted avg -> 115.0M Q3 FY26 avg -> 108.5M basic) because PTC spent $1,326M on buybacks in 9M FY26, partly funded by the $523M Kepware/ThingWorx sale proceeds and a $225M revolver draw.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30-Jun-2026 10-Q: LongTermDebt $1,398.2M (senior notes + term loan + ~$225M revolver drawn in Q3 FY26) + current portion $25.1M = $1,423.3M; cash $351.5M. Operating lease liabilities (~$172M at FY25) are NOT in net debt: under US GAAP the lease cost sits inside operating expense and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path (one lease treatment). Shares (29-Jul) are slightly later than the balance sheet (30-Jun); July buybacks reduced both cash and count, roughly offsetting.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL (10-K FY2025): ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back $216.2M + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $80.2M = $296.4M (summed: no combined company figure in the XBRL feed). 9M FY26: SBC $185.7M + withholding $67.3M = $253.0M (12.3% of 9M revenue, seasonally light quarter mix).
inputs.buyback_note: 9M FY26 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,326.2M (FY25 full year $300.0M). PTC is an active repurchaser, so the flat count is actually being funded -- and in FY26 more than funded (count shrinking well beyond SBC issuance, using divestiture proceeds and debt).
inputs.interest_expense_note: Interest expense $48.4M 9M FY26 (~$64M annualised). Net debt company, so interest income is immaterial and not deducted; the component build is unlevered (EBITDA-based) and the debt is deducted once in the bridge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 (large-cap industrial software, recurring but tied to manufacturing capex) -> cost of equity ~9.5%. Net debt ~$1.07B against ~$16B market cap (~6% weight) at ~5.5% after-tax -> WACC ~9.0%. Same 9.0% in every scenario: risk is charged once, in the scenario paths and weights, not via per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost inside opex, so inside the EBITDA margin; lease liabilities excluded from net debt. One treatment.
inputs.nci_treatment: None; PTC has no material non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (routing table row 1: operating software company; US filer, USD flows, no adaptations needed). First valuation of PTC -- no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF. MARGIN BASIS: the EBITDA margin path is CASH-CALIBRATED, not GAAP. Under ASC-606 PTC recognises multi-year term-licence revenue upfront, so revenue and GAAP EBITDA run ahead of cash collection: FY25 GAAP EBITDA was $1,084.9M (39.6%) or ~47.5% before SBC, yet unlevered owner FCF was only ~$615M (~22.5% of revenue). The path starts at 43.5% (pre-SBC) so that year-1 owner FCF lands near the FY26E cash run-rate (~$1.0B reported FCF less ~$320M SBC+withholding, ~25% of revenue), and a -10% working-capital capture on revenue growth charges the receivables build that comes with growth. DIVESTITURE: Kepware and ThingWorx (IIoT) sold to TPG, $523.3M cash received Q2 FY26; Q2 FY26 net income $590.7M is mostly the disposal gain and is excluded from every anchor. Revenue ex-divestiture is the CAD (Creo, Onshape) + PLM (Windchill, Codebeamer, ServiceMax) franchise. TAX: cash tax ramps 17% -> 21% (FY25 cash taxes $121.7M on ~$900M owner EBIT = ~13.5% after interest; OBBBA-2025 restoration of US R&D expensing keeps near-term cash tax low). D&A fades 3.4% -> 1.6% of revenue as acquired-intangible amortisation (ServiceMax, Arena, Codebeamer) rolls off, so the D&A tax shield is not perpetuated against 0.6% capex. Qualitative Analysis JSON was not yet written when this was built (parallel agent); scenario axes are drawn from the filings and the business mix.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: ARR-led forward growth (~7-9% constant-currency ARR growth in the FY26 framework), NOT the equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 21.6% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 13.4%; EPS (40.2%) and owner-FCF (54.0%) CAGRs are flattered by a low FY2020 base, ASC-606 term-licence timing, the ServiceMax (FY23) acquisition and the shrinking SBC share of revenue. None of them is a sustainable forward rate; the selected 8% follows ARR growth.
historical_growth.notes: Base years: FY2022 (3yr) and FY2020 (5yr) to FY2025. Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes (interest income nil, net debt): FY2020 $64.8M, FY2022 $171.9M, FY2025 $560.3M. Owner-FCF CAGR EXCEEDS reported FCF CAGR: SBC+withholding was roughly stable as a share of revenue (10.2% FY20, 10.8% FY25) and doubled in dollars ($148.9M -> $296.4M) while reported FCF quadrupled ($213.6M -> $856.7M), so stock is paying for a shrinking share of cash-flow growth. The 54% owner-FCF CAGR is a low-base artefact, not a forward rate.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 7%: ARR growth ~8% less the first-half drag of the divested Kepware/ThingWorx revenue. Then ~8% (ARR-led, CAD+PLM with price and SaaS migration) fading to 4% by FY36.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Cash-calibrated 43.5% (see inputs.notes) expanding ~3.5pp on operating leverage and the go-to-market restructuring, consistent with FCF margin rising from 28% (FY23) to 31% (FY25) reported.

scenario_narratives.base: PTC becomes a focused CAD + PLM franchise after selling Kepware/ThingWorx: Creo and Windchill are deeply embedded in discrete-manufacturing engineering workflows (switching means re-certifying product data and retraining engineers), so ARR compounds ~8% on price, seat expansion and the shift of on-premise Windchill/Creo to SaaS, decelerating to 4% by FY36 as the installed base matures. Cash margins expand ~3.5pp from the go-to-market restructuring and operating leverage, SBC+withholding glides from 11% to ~8.6% of revenue, and buybacks keep the count flat-to-down.
scenario_narratives.bull: PLM becomes the system of record for AI-driven product development: Windchill+Codebeamer (ALM) and ServiceMax win the digital-thread consolidation in aerospace/defence, automotive and medtech, Onshape takes cloud-native CAD share from SolidWorks/Fusion, and SaaS conversion lifts ARR growth to ~10-11% for several years. Pricing power plus a leaner cost base take cash EBITDA to 50%, and SBC falls to 8%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Industrial capex weakens (tariffs, auto/EV retrenchment, China) and the CAD/PLM duopoly with Dassault and Siemens turns more price-competitive just as AI-native design tools and Siemens' bundling compress seat growth. ARR growth slips to 3-4%, the SaaS migration costs margin rather than adding to it, and cash EBITDA drifts to 41% with SBC stuck near 10.5% of revenue to retain engineers.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the franchise is sticky and the balance sheet is fine (~1.1x EBITDA net debt), but PTC's growth is tied to discrete-manufacturing capex and the CAD market faces AI-native disruption. Base 50%: the ARR framework and FY23-FY25 cash-margin trend support it directly. Bull 30% (below 35%): it needs ARR acceleration AND further margin expansion AND SBC discipline together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a cash-calibrated margin: SBC and equity-award withholding fully expensed, share count held flat, ASC-606 upfront licence revenue not mistaken for cash. The divestiture gain and sale proceeds are excluded from the flows; their effect sits in the reduced share count and the June-2026 net-debt anchor.
key_risks_to_valuation: Base revenue is an FY26E estimate (Q4 FY26 not yet reported); a Q4 miss lowers the compounding base.
ASC-606 timing makes revenue lumpy; the margin path is calibrated to cash, so a reader comparing to GAAP EBITDA will see a ~5pp gap by design.
Debt-funded buybacks: net debt rose in FY26 even after $523M of divestiture proceeds.
Discrete-manufacturing cycle and tariffs on PTC's automotive/industrial customer base.
AI-native design tools and Siemens/Dassault bundling pressuring CAD seat growth.
